Lab Testing & Compliance SOPs — New Jersey (NJ-CRC · N.J.A.C. 17:30)

AreaProcedureNJ Rule
Pre-release testingBefore packaging/release, a licensed lab collects a representative initial + retention sample from each lot (statistically valid method). Do not sell until a written passing report is received.17:30-19
Test panelFull cannabinoid profile (THCA, THC, CBDA, CBD, CBGA, CBG, CBN, Δ8, THCV, CBC…) + terpenes (linalool, limonene, myrcene, caryophyllene, pinene…), plus contaminants per CRC Testing Guidance.CRC Testing Guidance
Failed testIf results don't meet spec: do not sell — destroy/dispose the lot and document disposal.17:30-19
Chain of custody / state QCMaintain sample chain of custody; CRC may collect samples for quality-control testing.17:30-19.1
Metrc complianceCreate test package & submit for required testing; record TestPassed before any transfer; only TestPassed packages may go on a transfer manifest.NJ Metrc Supp. Guide
LabelingCannabis item label must meet NJ requirements; anything not pre-printed on packaging goes on the batch sticker (see Labels tab + Packaging Guidelines).17:30-16.3
RecordkeepingRetain COAs and retention samples; keep batch/test records audit-ready.17:30

Growfather Gummy Production SOP (from SharePoint — Edition 1)

Source: SharePoint · "Gummy Depositing SOP.docx" + Recipe Cards. Approver: COO Chris Capurso. Terpenes = Abstrax (per-flavor recipe card). Dashboard COGS values take precedence over the 2024 recipe cards.
  • Equipment: Truffly Made depositor (8 pistons, 5 heat pads, nozzle/side/rear/front heaters), induction burner + double boiler per pot, thermometer/alarm, homogenizer, molds, sheet pans, bun racks.
  • Materials/pot: 10 kg gummy mix (1 Melt-to-Make box), THC oil (use Melt-to-Make calculator for dose — potency varies per oil batch), MCT oil, Abstrax flavor per recipe card, silicone + oil spray.
  • Prep: assemble + oil depositor (nozzles 195°, hopper 180°); double boiler 2–3" water on burner #6; load 10 kg pucks; thermometer alarm 165°; spray 42 molds w/ MCT.
  • Operation: melt to 165° (burner 12 → 6 + 10 min), skim bubbles (or weight fails testing), add THC + Abstrax flavor per recipe card, homogenize 30s (or mixer 3 min), deposit into sugared molds, level to flush.
  • Demold/cure: set 3–5 hrs (cold room ≤69°), press out onto sugar bin, fluff + coat, sift, single-layer cure overnight, then pack 10s into Growfather tins → packaging stage.
  • Other Growfather SOPs (from Recipe Sheet): 1g Disposable Vape (distillate fill + cap), 1.2g XL Quad Infused Preroll, Pectin Gummies, Chocolate Bar — author to match this format.

Naming & Batch ID Conventions

Standard (06/2026): every unit carries five layers — External (Metrc label) · Internal (Distru pick/assembly) · SKU (stable system key) · Lot/Batch (run trace) · Expiration (printed shelf date). The SKU never changes per batch — the Lot code carries the date, which keeps sales history, velocity, and forecasting intact. Applies to The Growfather, Little Leaf Labs Moonrock, Octane, and Dr. Zodiak's.

The Five-Layer Naming Standard

LayerPurposeFormatExample
ExternalLabel / Metrc / legal — what printsMost-recent approved Metrc Item Name (Metrc Item Export)1.2g (H) White Widow x Strawberry Cough Moonrock Infused Preroll XL
InternalDistru pick-pack & assembliesBrand | Weight | Subcategory | Flavor/Strain | IHSGF | 1.2g | Infused Preroll | White Widow x Strawberry Cough | H
SKU (stable)System key — never changes per batchBRAND-WEIGHT-PRODUCT-FLAVORGF-1.2G-INFPR-WWSC
Lot / BatchTraces the production run (immutable)YYMM + run letter = production/test month2605A (1st May-2026 run; B = 2nd)
ExpirationPrinted shelf date — editable on relabeltest date + 6 mo → extend 12/18 mo on relabel2026-11 → 2027-05 (lot stays 2605A)
Why the date is NOT in the SKU: a dated SKU makes every batch a new "product," fragmenting sales history and breaking per-SKU velocity/forecast. The SKU identifies what it is; the Lot identifies which run. Expiration is derived (test+6mo) and bumped on relabel — the lot code never moves, so traceability is preserved while the printed date floats.

Lot / Batch Code Convention

Lot Code Format (new standard)

FORMAT
[SKU] · Lot YYMM + run letter
Lot: 2605A = 1st production/test run of May 2026 · 2605B = 2nd run that month. Encodes the immutable production/test date.
Full unit ID: GF-1.2G-INFPR-WWSC · 2605A — SKU never changes; only the lot increments per run.
Expiration: derived = test date + 6 mo. On relabel, extend to 12 or 18 mo — update the printed Expiration field only; the lot code stays 2605A so traceability is preserved.
Old format being retired: the MM/YY batch string (e.g. MR-INF-01/26) folds into the immutable Lot + the SKU.
Confirm the YYMM lot format meets NJ-CRC / NJ Metrc traceability with the Little Leaf Labs compliance lead before going live.

3-Week Material Requirements (from BOM) + Packaging Lead Time

For SKUs ≤3 weeks of cover, the BOM is exploded to confirm cannabis + non-cannabis materials are on hand to run the batch. Packaging from China has a 4–6 week lead time — order packaging for the next batch when starting the current one.

Production Intelligence — Batch Status & Forecast Rules

Batch status definitions
  • WIP Batch — manufacturing / assembly / testing pending / testing submitted. Active production inventory.
  • Label Batch — testing PASSED, awaiting labeling / packaging / final release. NOT finished goods — remains an Active Production Batch and must appear on the Production, Active Batch, and Inventory Forecast views. Do not remove from production reporting.
  • Ready For Sale (RFS) — tested, labeled, packaged, released to inventory. Only RFS is sellable inventory.
Label batch naming standard — Brand | Product Line | Strain/Flavor | Batch # | Mfg Date. e.g. Growfather | Sour Diesel | Moonrock Preroll | Batch 2605-01. Flag batches missing Strain/Flavor/Product Name as Production Data Errors.
Triggers: create a WIP batch when Weeks Remaining ≤ 3 (with material + labor requirements + expected completion); submit testing at ≈ 1 week of cover so results return before depletion.
Priority order: 1) Unit velocity · 2) Weeks remaining · 3) Gross-profit contribution. A 1,500-unit/mo preroll outranks a 150-unit/mo vape even if the vape earns more revenue.
Daily exec questions: Which SKUs run out first? Which need WIP this week? Which to submit for testing? Which await labels? Which active batches are stuck? What to schedule next? What inventory risk exists in the next 6 weeks?

SKU ↔ Metrc Item Map & Naming Conventions

Metrc is the canonical name source; Distru mirrors it. Two conventions below — official (external/Metrc) and internal — plus the SKU-code standard. Map ties every internal SKU to its official Metrc/Distru name, brand, subcategory, flavor, IHS class, and weight.

Naming Conventions

Official (Metrc / Distru): Brand | Subcategory | Flavor | IHS | Weight  —  e.g. Dr. Zodiak#As Moonrocks | Snowballz | Razzle Dazzle | (H) | 2g
Internal use: Weight | Subcategory | Flavor | IHS | Brand Abbrev (GF / DR.Z / OCT / SH)  —  e.g. 2g | Snowballz | Razzle Dazzle | H | DR.Z
IHS = Indica (I) / Hybrid (H) / Sativa (S). (Mo/Year) = batch month/year suffix.
SKU code standard:
  • GF Vapes 1g/2g: GF-1G-Vape-Trop-(mo/yr) · GF-2g-Vape-SourD-(mo/yr)
  • Growfather Preroll 1.2g: GF-PR-120-GDP-(mo/yr)
  • Growfather Gummy: GF-GM-Dream-(mo/yr)
  • Growfather Chocolate: GF-Choc-PBCup-(mo/yr)
  • Dr. Zodiak: Dr-BUCK-FW-Razzle-4g · Dr-Buck-Snow-BobbyB-2g · Dr-Snow-LynLem-2g · Dr-Fuzzy-Ghost-3.5g · Dr-PR-NiteOwl-1.4g · Dr-MoonDust-1g (all +(Mo/Year))

What this dashboard is built on

Transparency on data sources and how to unlock the full spec.

This dashboard runs on your Lit Alerts market-intelligence exports (Jan 1 – May 31, 2026): estimated units, price, value, and market share for the entire New Jersey market, sliced by brand, category, dispensary, and day. That makes the Brand Health & Market Traction view — your #1 priority — fully live today: you can see exactly where Growfather, Octane, and Dr. Zodiak stand against 657 competing brands.

✓ Live now (from Lit Alerts)
  • Brand market share, units, value & competitive rank
  • Category share & market structure
  • Dispensary / account landscape & targeting
  • Market daily trend (30/60-day)
  • Premium vs volume positioning
⚠ Needs internal data to activate
  • Stores Added / Lost & Net Store Growth (needs period-over-period)
  • Account revenue, A/R balance, gross profit (Back Office)
  • Days since last order, repeat-order rate (orders data)
  • Revenue vs goal, sales-by-rep (CRM / sales log)
  • Promotion ROI, forecast demand (promo & inventory feeds)
Two data notes:
  • Sugar High and Moonrock had no measurable sales in the NJ market export for this period — likely pre-launch or tracked under a different name. They'll appear automatically once they show market activity.
  • A reliable 90-day trend needs 180 days of history; this export covers 151 days, so only 30- and 60-day trends are shown. The full 90-day view unlocks once a longer export window is available.

↗ Expansion Opportunities — Current Buyers

Active buyers only, sized against their total store sell-through. Tracks 90-day-over-90-day and month-over-month growth with us and flags the Little Leaf categories with the most headroom. SKU-level potential needs Distru line items (see note).

Penetration = our 2026 sales ÷ the store's total retail sell-through (Lit Alerts). Category fit suggests which Little Leaf lines to push based on market category strength. Exact SKU gaps need Distru line-item data — once connected, this shows precisely which SKUs each store doesn't yet carry.

Data sources & method

Live as of June 1, 2026.
✓ Connected
  • Distru — 1,291 orders (2024-26), 173 accounts: revenue, $1K+ cadence, recency, new/recovered/lost
  • QuickBooks — sales by customer + A/R aging ($420.9K receivable)
  • Lit Alerts — 657 brands, 294 dispensaries, categories, daily trend
  • CCA — credit aging (90+ = bad, 60-90 = watch)
⚠ Add to complete the spec
  • Distru line items — SKU per order → brand distribution, avg order & frequency per brand, exact SKU white-space
  • Metrc — confirm shipped units & per-brand placement by store
  • Period-over-period Lit Alerts — brand MoM units/sales growth (currently one snapshot)
  • Category-segmented Lit Alerts export — top-20 brands per category & penetration
Logic: Serviced/lapsed/cadence use orders >$1,000 only. Lapsed = no $1K+ order in 90+ days. Targets = $500K+/mo stores never-sold or lapsed 90+. Credit: 90+ = bad, 60-90 = watch. Reviewed Mondays & Thursdays (scheduled).
Little Leaf Sales Command Center · Notes saved locally in your browser · Market values = modeled retail sell-through; revenue = booked wholesale.
